steps.text: Combine onion, vinegar, honey, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and pepper flakes in a blender; blend on high, gradually adding olive oil until puréed. Continue blending until thick, about 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Balsamic Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This honey balsamic vinaigrette recipe, with onion, garlic, red pepper flakes, soy sauce, honey, and sugar was inspired by the one from TGI Fridays.
raw_recipe.name: Honey Balsamic Vinaigrette

recipeInstructions.text: Combine onion, vinegar, honey, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and pepper flakes in a blender; blend on high, gradually adding olive oil until puréed. Continue blending until thick, about 2 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is the best dressing - it's absolutely perfect as-is. My favorite salad to put it on is the Pecan Crusted Chicken Salad by Lianad on this site. Thanks for sharing you're hard work sleuthing the recipe!

I could drink this. I did not measure, I approximated into my BlendTec using dried minced onions, 2 garlic cloves, a couple long squeezes of raw local honey, a few grinds of Trader Joe's seasoning that has mustard seed, pepper, salt and some other herbs, a handful of shakes if red pepper flakes. I forgot sugar, but didn't need it. After well blending I poured in the olive oil while it was blending... it turned creamy from emulsifying. I love sweet balsamic, so it worked for us.

My FB post - Delisciousness... over baby spinach, rotisserie chicken, raspberries, blueberries, blue cheese, and chopped cinnamon almonds. Wish I took a picture. Hubby went for 2nds.

This is delicious!!! I followed to the “T” and I added 2 Tablespoons of Dijon Mustard to help cut the strong vinegar taste and to help emulsify ...it is outstanding...gotta give it a try....
Thank you for sharing this

Amazing!!! I used a shallot instead of onion (its what I had), and didn't add sugar initially - instead I added afterward to taste - ended up probably using 2 tsp. Made in advance, threw in the fridge, and just shook up vigorously before serving over a bed of mixed greens with golden raisins and toasted almonds. Side note: I've only used "golden balsamic vinegar" so far to make this... haven't tried with regular balsamic.

I really like the mix of flavors, the only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because it was a little sweet for my taste. But I'm more of a savory person. Knowing that I omitted the sugar and only used honey, but was still a bit sweet for me. Next time I will add only 1 or 1 1/2 T of honey. My family loved it the way it was.

Red pepper flakes are a great change/addition to this recipe! I accidentally bought honey goat cheese and included about a tablespoon in the dressing and it tasted great and got a bit creamy! It was great over any salad, especially one with spinach, strawberries, honey goat cheese and French fried jalapeños. Yum!

This is a really nice dressing. I used a small shallot and did not blend the ingredients (didn't feel like making more dirty dishes). I eyeballed most of the ingredients, used a little less oil, left out the sugar, and I think this recipe is really easy to customize to your own taste. Definitely will make again since it's quick, delicious and I usually have the ingredients on-hand

This is great! Like all dressings it's to taste. I only used 1/4 c oil and rest water. I added 1T miso paste and probably 2T of raw cashews to give it some creaminess. This is a great recipe with changes or stand alone.

This makes a lot of dressing so I halve the recipe. Also, the sugar should be added to taste as it can be very sweet. Serve it on a romaine and spinach salad with some toasted pecans and it is delicious. Golden raisins are also a nice addition and the dressing can also be used as a amarinade. And, finally, if you are out of garlic you can use jarred and diced garlic.

My God this is so delicious.
The only thing I didn't exactly follow was the onion. I used a red/purple onion. It was a large one so I used a 1/3 of it.
Amazing salad dressing!
Keeping and using it again. Now I will for sure be making more Spinach Salads.
Best balsamic ever. I reverse the balsamic and olive oil. I also have used avocado oil and its excellent!

It's been 5 years since I discovered this recipe and I have made it more times than I can count. The original recipe as written is perfection and I find myself using this as a marinade, a dressing, and a dip! Super easy to make and the flavors meld together nicely. Definitely a keeper!
I actually split the honey with regular honey and Mike’s hot honey, equal parts. Gives it a little kick. My husband loved it!

This is a very nice vinaigrette which is a little tangy but with a good balance of sweet-sour. Enjoyed for lunch on a mixed greens salad with red onions, cucumber, dried cranberries, and some Club crackers. Might be interesting to try this with milder white balsamic vinegar for a variation. Made half a recipe and definitely would make again.
Loved this! Used my hand blender. Made a little over a carafe full. Enjoyed it over Italian grilled chicken salad and beef fajita salad. Very, very good!
I replaced the sugar Aguava and used coconut aminos instead of soy sauce. Also, added a touch of lime.
A very good and simple dressing. It went over a romaine, chicken, pear, apple, and feta salad. Wonderful flavor.

I had to reduce the quantities as it was just for the two of us and I didn't want have more in case it wasn't something we enjoyed. in the end it was amazing, will add pine seeds next time because I intend to make it again.
We love this dressing! I marinated my salmon fillet with this and also used some of the dressing over the greens I had with the salmon. It was delicious...and I didn’t change a thing.
